name: Kulpakji Jain Bhojanalaya
area: Kolanupaka Jain Temple complex, Aler mandal
signature_dish: Jain vegetarian meal cooked to Jain dietary principles
why_it_matters: The bhojanalaya inside the Kolanupaka (Kulpakji) Jain temple — a roughly 2,000-year-old Svetambara Jain shrine, 80km from Hyderabad on NH-163. The dining hall serves breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks free to visitors (around 100 meals a day, donations accepted), with food prepared strictly to Jain customs — no root vegetables, no after-dark cooking. In a village with almost no commercial dining, it is the genuine anchor.
insider_tip: The bhojanalaya is the meal at Kolanupaka — eat here after temple darshan. Food follows Jain rules: pure-veg, no onion-garlic, no root vegetables. Leave a donation. For anything else you will need to drive to Aler or Jangaon.
signature_address: Kolanupaka Jain Temple (Kulpakji), Kolanupaka village, Aler mandal, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana 508126

name: Seasons Family Restaurant (Jangaon base)
why_it_matters: A family restaurant in Jangaon town — the nearest place with a proper sit-down meal to Kolanupaka, about 13km away. Kolanupaka village itself has no commercial restaurant, so Jangaon is the practical base-town option for visitors who want a non-temple meal.
insider_tip: This is a Jangaon base-town pick, not in Kolanupaka itself — useful if you have eaten light at the temple bhojanalaya and want biryani or grills afterwards. Walk-in.

name: Nine Dine Restaurant (Jangaon base)
area: Balaji Nagar, Jangaon town (~13km from Kolanupaka)
why_it_matters: A biryani-and-mandi restaurant in Jangaon's Balaji Nagar — another Jangaon base-town option for Kolanupaka visitors. With biryani, mandi and Chinese, it is a dependable casual meal in the nearest town to the Jain temple village.
insider_tip: A Jangaon base-town option for Kolanupaka. The mandi is the less-usual order alongside the standard biryani. Walk-in.
signature_address: Balaji Nagar, Jangaon town, Jangaon District, Telangana 506167
